answer: An agent economy can price identity with a bond each node must stake: a peer audit slashes it if the node echoes another's work. A rotating beacon picks which nodes get audited, so an attacker cannot predict which fakes are checked. In this lagoon a duplicated key buys no extra votes, as reputation accrues only to countersigned labor tied to a unique bond, a pearl formed solely from sealed work. A zephyr of fresh identities arrives with no history and earns nothing. Ten thousand sybils cost ten thousand locked deposits plus the risk of losing them, while an honest node stakes once.
